p.src: When Baoyu heard this, he hurried inside to see what was wanted and found Hupo standing before the screen. “Hurry along,” she said. “They are waiting for you to speak.” Baoyu went to the main apartments and found Grandmother Jia discussing with Lady Wang and the young ladies how they should return Shi Xiangyun’s hospitality. Baoyu said, “I have an idea. Since there will be no outside guests, there is no need to prescribe a fixed number of dishes. We could simply prepare a few of whatever each person usually likes. Instead of setting formal tables, we could place a tall side table before each person, with one or two favorite dishes, a compartmented box of assorted delicacies, and a winepot for each to pour from. Would that not be something different?” Grandmother Jia approved at once and promptly ordered word sent to the kitchen: “Tomorrow, prepare the things we like to eat, and pack boxes according to the number of people. We shall have breakfast in the garden as well.” While they were still discussing the arrangements, the lamps were lit. The night passed without incident.

p.src: Early the next morning, they arose to find, happily, that the day was clear and bright. Li Wan rose before everyone else and supervised the old women and maids as they swept up the fallen leaves, wiped the tables and chairs, and prepared the tea and wine utensils. Presently Feng’er came in with Granny Liu and Ban’er. “You are certainly busy, Mistress Li,” she said. Li Wan laughed. “I told you yesterday that you would not manage to leave, but you were so intent on going.” Granny Liu laughed. “The Old Lady asked me to stay and join the merriment for another day.” Feng’er produced several keys of different sizes and said, “Our mistress says there may not be enough tall tables outside. We had better open the pavilion and bring down those stored upstairs for the day. Our mistress ought to have come herself, but she is speaking with Her Ladyship, so she asks Mistress Li to unlock the place and have the servants carry them down.” Li Wan told Suyun to take the keys, then sent an old woman to summon several pages from the inner gate. Standing below the Grand Prospect Pavilion, Li Wan looked up and ordered someone to open the Brocade-Adorned Gallery and bring the tables down one by one. The pages, old women, and maids all lent a hand and carried down more than twenty tables. “Take care,” Li Wan warned. “Do not rush about as though demons were chasing you. Mind you do not damage the carved edges.” Then she turned to Granny Liu and said with a smile, “Granny, why do you not go up and have a look too?” Granny Liu was delighted to hear the invitation. Taking Ban’er by the hand, she immediately climbed the stairs. Inside, she saw dim masses of folding screens, tables, chairs, lanterns large and small, and other such objects. Though she knew little of what they were, their dazzling colors and wondrous designs filled her eyes. After invoking the Buddha several times, she went back down. The doors were then locked, and everyone came downstairs. Li Wan said, “The Old Lady may feel inclined to go boating. We might as well bring down the punts, poles, oars, and sun awnings and have them ready.” The servants assented, reopened the storehouse, and brought down every kind of equipment. The pages were told to summon the boatwomen and have them pole two boats out from the boathouse. Amid the bustle of these arrangements, Grandmother Jia appeared, leading a large company into the garden. Li Wan hurried forward to meet her and said with a smile, “You must indeed be in high spirits, Old Ancestress, to have come in already. I thought you would not yet have dressed your hair, so I had just picked some chrysanthemums to send to you.” As she spoke, Biyue came forward holding a large emerald-green platter shaped like a lotus leaf, filled with cut sprays of chrysanthemums in many colors. Grandmother Jia selected a large crimson bloom and pinned it above her temple. Turning and catching sight of Granny Liu, she laughed. “Come here and put on some flowers.” Before she had finished speaking, Xifeng pulled Granny Liu over and said with a laugh, “Let me dress you up.” With that, she stuck the whole platterful of flowers all over Granny Liu’s head, this way and that. Grandmother Jia and all the others laughed uncontrollably.

p.src: Talking and laughing, they soon reached the Pavilion of Seeping Fragrance. The maids brought a large brocade cushion and spread it over the bench beside the railing. Grandmother Jia sat leaning against a pillar and ordered Granny Liu to sit beside her. Then she asked, “What do you think of this garden?” Invoking the Buddha, Granny Liu replied, “At New Year, we country folk all go into town to buy pictures to paste on our walls. Whenever we have leisure, we often say to one another how wonderful it would be if we could step into those pictures and stroll about. We always thought those scenes were no more than inventions, for where could such a place exist in real life? Who would have thought that when I entered this garden today and saw it for myself, it would prove ten times finer than any picture! If only someone would paint this garden for me, so that I could take the picture home and show it to everyone! Then even if I died, the sight of it would have done me good.” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia pointed to Xichun and said with a smile, “Look at this little granddaughter of mine. She knows how to paint. How would it be if I asked her to paint one for you tomorrow?” Granny Liu was overjoyed. She hurried over, took Xichun by the hand, and cried, “My dear young lady! So young, so pretty, and gifted with such skill as well—surely you must be an immortal reborn!”

p.src: After Grandmother Jia had rested awhile, she naturally led Grannie Liu around to see all the sights. Their first stop was the Naiad's House. As they entered, they saw green bamboo lining both sides of the path, moss carpeting the ground, and a narrow, winding pebble path running through the middle. Grannie Liu stepped aside to let Grandmother Jia and the others use the path, while she herself hurried along over the bare ground. Amber took her arm and said, “Grannie, come up onto the path. Mind you don't slip on the moss.” “Never mind me,” said Grannie Liu. “We're used to walking over ground like this. You young ladies just keep to the path. It would be a shame to soil those embroidered shoes of yours.” Intent on talking to those above her, she failed to watch her footing, slipped as predicted, and fell with a thump. Everyone clapped their hands and burst into laughter. Grandmother Jia laughingly scolded them: “You little wretches! Help her up instead of standing there laughing.” By the time she spoke, Grannie Liu had already scrambled to her feet. Laughing too, she said, “No sooner had I boasted than I made a liar of myself.” Grandmother Jia asked her, “Have you twisted your back? Let the maids give it a rub.” “What makes you think I'm so delicate?” replied Grannie Liu. “There's hardly a day when I don't take a tumble or two. If I needed rubbing down every time, what would become of me?” Zijuan had already raised the spotted-bamboo blind, and Grandmother Jia and the others went inside and sat down. Lin Daiyu personally brought Grandmother Jia a covered cup of tea on a small tray. Lady Wang said, “We shall not take tea, child, so there is no need to pour any.” On hearing this, Lin Daiyu told a maid to move the chair in which she usually sat by the window to a lower place and invited Lady Wang to sit there. Seeing brushes and an inkstone on the desk beneath the window and shelves piled full of books, Grannie Liu said, “This must be some young gentleman's study.” Grandmother Jia pointed at Daiyu with a smile. “This is my granddaughter's room.” Grannie Liu looked Daiyu over carefully before smiling and saying, “Why, this is nothing like a young lady's boudoir. It is finer even than the best gentleman's study.” Grandmother Jia then asked, “Why haven't we seen Baoyu?” The maids answered, “He is in a boat on the pond.” “Who had a boat made ready?” asked Grandmother Jia. Li Wan hastened to reply, “When we opened the storied building just now to fetch the small tables, I thought Your Ladyship might be in the mood for it, so I had one prepared.” Grandmother Jia was about to speak when someone announced, “Aunt Xue has arrived.” Grandmother Jia and the others had only just risen when Aunt Xue came in. As they resumed their seats, she smiled and said, “Your Ladyship is in such high spirits today that you have come out this early.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “I was just saying that anyone who came late should be punished, and now, Aunt, you are the one who has arrived late.”

p.src: After they had chatted and laughed awhile, Grandmother Jia noticed that the gauze on the windows had faded and said to Lady Wang, “This gauze looks pretty when first pasted on, but after a while it loses its fresh green color. There are no peach or apricot trees in this courtyard, and the bamboo is green already, so green gauze on the windows does not suit it at all. I remember we used to have window gauze in four or five different colors. Tomorrow, have this replaced for her.” Xifeng hurriedly said, “When I opened the storeroom yesterday, I saw several bolts of silver-red cicada-wing gauze in a large chest. Some had sprays of flowers, some had floating-cloud and endless-fortune patterns, and some had a hundred butterflies flitting among flowers. The colors were so brilliant and the gauze so light and soft that I had never seen anything like it. I took out two bolts to make two quilt covers, thinking the material must be exceptionally fine.” Grandmother Jia laughed when she heard this. “Pooh! Everyone says there is nothing you haven't experienced or seen, yet you cannot even recognize this gauze. You had better not boast again.” Aunt Xue and the others laughed too. “However experienced and knowledgeable she may be, how could she compare with Your Ladyship? Why not instruct her, Your Ladyship, and let us learn something too?” Xifeng also laughed. “Dear Ancestress, do teach me.” Grandmother Jia smiled at Aunt Xue and the others. “That gauze is older than any of you. No wonder she mistook it for cicada-wing gauze, since it does resemble it somewhat. Anyone unfamiliar with it would make the same mistake. Its proper name is ‘Soft-Smoke Gauze.’” “That is a lovely name,” said Xifeng. “Yet although I am fully grown and have seen hundreds of kinds of gauze and silk, I have never heard this name before.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “How long have you lived? You have seen only a few rare things and already you boast about it. Soft-Smoke Gauze comes in only four colors: clear-sky-after-rain blue, autumn-incense yellow, pine green, and silver-red. When it is made into bed curtains or pasted over window frames, it looks like mist or smoke from a distance, which is why it is called ‘Soft-Smoke Gauze.’ The silver-red variety is also called ‘Sunset-Cloud Gauze.’ Even the official gauze made for imperial use nowadays is not so soft, substantial, light, and finely woven.” Aunt Xue laughed. “Never mind that Xifeng has not seen it—even I have never heard of it.” Even as Xifeng spoke, she had already ordered someone to fetch a bolt. Grandmother Jia said, “Yes, this is the very thing! At first it was used only for covering window frames, but later we tried making quilts and bed curtains from it, and it proved excellent for those as well. Tomorrow, find several bolts and use the silver-red gauze to cover her windows.” Xifeng promised that she would. Everyone examined the gauze and praised it without end.

p.src: Granny Liu, too, could not take her squinting eyes off it. Invoking the Buddha's name, she said, “We could never hope to make clothes from such stuff, yet you use it to paste over windows. What a pity!” Lady Jia said, “It would not look good made into clothes.” Xifeng hurriedly pulled out the front of the bright-red padded gauze jacket she was wearing and said to Lady Jia and Aunt Xue, “Just look at this jacket of mine.” Lady Jia and Aunt Xue both said, “This is of the finest quality too. It was made recently in the imperial workshops for palace use, yet it cannot compare with that.” Xifeng said, “This flimsy stuff is still called palace-made for imperial use, but it cannot even compare with material made for officials.” Lady Jia said, “Look again. I believe there may be some blue material as well. If there is, bring it all out. Give two lengths to our kinswoman Liu so that she can make a bed curtain for me to hang, then line what remains and make some lined waistcoats for the maids. There is no sense storing it until it grows mildewed and rots.” Xifeng promptly assented and had the material taken away again. Lady Jia rose and said with a smile, “This room is cramped. Let us go and look around elsewhere.” Invoking the Buddha's name, Granny Liu said, “Everyone says that great families live in great houses. Yesterday I saw Your Ladyship's main apartments, furnished with enormous trunks, cupboards, tables, and beds. They were imposing indeed. That cupboard is taller and larger than a whole room in our house. No wonder there was a ladder in the rear courtyard. I wondered why you kept a ladder when you did not climb onto the roof to dry things. Then it occurred to me that it must be for opening the upper cupboards and putting things in or taking them out. How could anyone reach them without that ladder? And now that I have seen this little room, I find it even more perfectly arranged than the large one. Everything in the room is lovely, though I do not know what any of it is called. The more I look, the less I can bear to leave.” Xifeng said, “There are finer things yet. I shall take you to see them all.” With that, they left the Xiaoxiang Lodge and went on their way.

p.src: From afar they saw a group of people poling boats on the pond. Lady Jia said, “Since they have prepared the boats, let us ride in them.” As she spoke, they made their way toward the area around Amaranth Isle and Smartweed Bank. Before they reached the pond, they saw several old serving-women approaching, each carrying an identical large multicolored box decorated with pinched wire and incised gold. Xifeng quickly asked Lady Wang where breakfast was to be laid. Lady Wang replied, “Ask where the Old Lady wishes to dine, and lay it there.” Hearing this, Lady Jia turned and said, “Your third younger sister's place will do nicely. Take the servants and lay the meal there. We shall go from here by boat.” At this, Xifeng turned back and, accompanied by Tanchun, Li Wan, Yuanyang, Amber, and the servants carrying the food, took a shortcut to Autumn Freshness Studio, where they arranged the tables in Dawn-Jade Hall. Yuanyang said with a laugh, “Every day we talk about how the gentlemen outside always keep some sponger at their drinking parties and meals to serve as the butt of their jokes. Today we have found ourselves a female sponger too.” Li Wan was an honest, straightforward soul and did not understand what she meant. Xifeng, however, knew that she meant Granny Liu and said with a laugh, “Then today we shall use her to make some fun.” The two of them then whispered together and settled their scheme. Li Wan smilingly remonstrated, “You two never do a single good deed! You are not children anymore, yet you are still so mischievous. Take care, or the Old Lady will scold you.” Yuanyang laughed. “It has nothing whatever to do with you. I shall take responsibility.” While they were still speaking, Lady Jia and the others arrived and seated themselves wherever they pleased. First, the maids were told to bring two trays of tea, which everyone drank. Xifeng held a foreign-cloth napkin wrapped around a bundle of ebony chopsticks inlaid with silver in three places. Counting out the places, she set a pair at each seat. Lady Jia then said, “Bring that little nanmu table over here, so that our kinswoman Liu may sit near me.” At her words, the servants hurriedly carried it over. Xifeng signaled to Yuanyang with her eyes. Yuanyang drew Granny Liu outside, secretly gave her a long set of instructions, and added, “These are the rules of our household. If you make a mistake, we shall laugh at you.” When all had been arranged, they returned to their seats. Aunt Xue had already eaten before coming and took no food, but sat to one side drinking tea. Lady Jia shared one table with Baoyu, Xiangyun, Daiyu, and Baochai. Lady Wang shared another table with Yingchun and her two sisters, while Granny Liu had a separate table beside Lady Jia. Ordinarily, when Lady Jia ate, young maids stood beside her holding such articles as a rinsing bowl, a yak-tail whisk, and towels. Yuanyang no longer performed this duty, but today she deliberately took the yak-tail whisk and stood there waving it. The maids knew that she meant to make sport of Granny Liu, so they withdrew and left the way clear for her.

Hearing this, Lady Jia turned and said, “Your third younger sister's place will do nicely.
Take the servants and lay the meal there. We shall go from here by boat.”

At this, Xifeng turned back and, accompanied by Tanchun, Li Wan, Yuanyang, Amber, and the servants carrying the food, took a shortcut to Autumn Freshness Studio, where they arranged the tables in Dawn-Jade Hall.
Yuanyang said with a laugh, “Every day we talk about how the gentlemen outside always keep some sponger at their drinking parties and meals to serve as the butt of their jokes.
Today we have found ourselves a female sponger too.”
Li Wan was an honest, straightforward soul and did not understand what she meant.
Xifeng, however, knew that she meant Granny Liu and said with a laugh, “Then today we shall use her to make some fun.”
The two of them then whispered together and settled their scheme.
Li Wan smilingly remonstrated, “You two never do a single good deed! You are not children anymore, yet you are still so mischievous. Take care, or the Old Lady will scold you.”
Yuanyang laughed. “It has nothing whatever to do with you. I shall take responsibility.”
While they were still speaking, Lady Jia and the others arrived and seated themselves wherever they pleased.
First, the maids were told to bring two trays of tea, which everyone drank.
Xifeng held a foreign-cloth napkin wrapped around a bundle of ebony chopsticks inlaid with silver in three places. Counting out the places, she set a pair at each seat.
Lady Jia then said, “Bring that little nanmu table over here, so that our kinswoman Liu may sit near me.”
At her words, the servants hurriedly carried it over.

Xifeng signaled to Yuanyang with her eyes. Yuanyang drew Granny Liu outside, secretly gave her a long set of instructions, and added, “These are the rules of our household. If you make a mistake, we shall laugh at you.”
When all had been arranged, they returned to their seats.
Aunt Xue had already eaten before coming and took no food, but sat to one side drinking tea.
Lady Jia shared one table with Baoyu, Xiangyun, Daiyu, and Baochai.
Lady Wang shared another table with Yingchun and her two sisters, while Granny Liu had a separate table beside Lady Jia.
Ordinarily, when Lady Jia ate, young maids stood beside her holding such articles as a rinsing bowl, a yak-tail whisk, and towels.
Yuanyang no longer performed this duty, but today she deliberately took the yak-tail whisk and stood there waving it.
The maids knew that she meant to make sport of Granny Liu, so they withdrew and left the way clear for her.

p.src: As Yuanyang stood in attendance, she whispered to Granny Liu, “Do not forget.” Granny Liu replied, “Do not worry, miss.” When Granny Liu had taken her seat and picked up her chopsticks, she found them so heavy and unwieldy that they would not sit properly in her hand. At the sight of them, Granny Liu said, “These little pitchforks are heavier than the iron shovel back home. How am I ever to manage them?” Her words made everyone burst out laughing.

p.src: A married maidservant stood there holding a food box. A young maid came forward and removed its lid, revealing two bowls of food inside. Li Wan took one bowl and placed it on Lady Jia's table. Xifeng deliberately chose the bowl of pigeon eggs and set it on Grandmother Liu's table. When Lady Jia said, “Please begin,” Grandmother Liu rose and loudly declared, “Old Liu, old Liu, eats as much as any ox; she could gobble a whole old sow without once lifting her head.” Then she puffed out her cheeks and fell silent. Everyone stared in bewilderment at first, but once they understood, high and low alike burst into peals of laughter. Shi Xiangyun could contain herself no longer and sprayed out a mouthful of rice. Lin Daiyu laughed until she lost her breath and leaned over the table crying, “Oh, dear!” Baoyu had already tumbled into Lady Jia's arms, and she clasped him to her, laughing and calling him her darling. Lady Wang pointed at Xifeng but was laughing too hard to speak. Aunt Xue likewise lost control and sprayed a mouthful of tea all over Tanchun's skirt. Tanchun tipped her rice bowl onto Yingchun, while Xichun left her seat, tugged at her nurse, and begged her to rub her aching belly. Not one of the servants below remained upright: some slipped outside to squat and laugh, while others suppressed their mirth long enough to come forward and change their young mistresses' clothes. Only Xifeng and Yuanyang held firm and continued urging Grandmother Liu to eat. Grandmother Liu picked up the chopsticks, but found that they would not obey her hand. “Even the chickens here are dainty,” she said. “No wonder the eggs they lay are so tiny and pretty. Let me spear one and gobble it up.” Everyone had only just stopped laughing, but at these words they began all over again. Lady Jia laughed until tears streamed down her face, while Hupo stood behind her patting her back. “This must be some mischief of that imp Xifeng's,” Lady Jia said with a laugh. “You mustn't believe what she tells you.” Grandmother Liu was still praising the daintiness of the eggs and saying she would spear one when Xifeng laughed and said, “They cost a tael of silver apiece. Hurry and taste one; they won't be good once they're cold.” Grandmother Liu reached in with her chopsticks, but there was no picking one up. After chasing them all around the bowl, she finally managed with great difficulty to scoop one up. She had just craned her neck to eat it when it slipped away and rolled onto the floor. She hastily put down her chopsticks to retrieve it herself, but one of the attendants had already picked it up and carried it away. Grandmother Liu sighed. “A whole tael of silver gone without so much as a sound!” By now no one had any thought of eating; they were all watching her and laughing. Lady Jia spoke again. “Why have you brought out those chopsticks now, when we aren't holding a grand banquet for formal guests? This is all Xifeng's doing. Why haven't you changed them yet?” The attendants had not originally prepared the ivory chopsticks; Xifeng and Yuanyang had brought them themselves. Hearing this, they hurriedly removed them and replaced them, as with the others, with a pair of ebony chopsticks inlaid with silver.

p.src: When the meal was over, Lady Jia and the others went to Tanchun's bedroom to chat. The remains of the meal were cleared away here, and another table was laid. Watching Li Wan and Xifeng sit opposite each other to eat, Grandmother Liu sighed. “Never mind everything else; what I admire most is the way things are done in your household. No wonder people say, ‘True manners come from great houses.’” Xifeng hastened to say with a smile, “Please don't take it to heart. Just now everyone was only having a little fun.” Before she had finished, Yuanyang came in too and said with a smile, “Don't be angry, Granny. I owe you an apology.” Grandmother Liu laughed. “What are you saying, miss? We were putting on a little show to cheer the old lady. Why would I be angry? You warned me beforehand, so I understood that it was only to give everyone a laugh. If I had been offended, I simply wouldn't have said any of it.” Yuanyang then scolded the servants: “Why hasn't anyone poured tea for Granny?” Grandmother Liu hurriedly said, “That woman poured me some tea just now, and I've already had it. You ought to have your meal too, miss.” Xifeng took Yuanyang by the hand. “Sit down and eat with us. It will save us from having another commotion later.” So Yuanyang sat down. The older servants brought another bowl and pair of chopsticks, and the three finished their meal. Grandmother Liu laughed. “I see that all of you eat only that tiny amount and then stop. It's a wonder you aren't hungry. No wonder they say even a gust of wind could blow you over.” Yuanyang asked, “There was quite a lot of food left today. Where has it all gone?” The older servants replied, “It hasn't been distributed yet. We're keeping it here until we can divide it among them all at once.” “They won't be able to eat all this,” said Yuanyang. “Choose two bowls and send them to Ping'er in Second Mistress's rooms.” “She has already eaten,” said Xifeng. “There's no need to send her any.” “If she doesn't want it, she can feed it to your cats,” said Yuanyang. Hearing this, one of the older servants hurriedly selected two dishes, put them in a box, and sent them over. Yuanyang asked, “Where has Suyun gone?” “They are all eating together here,” said Li Wan. “What do you need her for?” “Then never mind,” said Yuanyang. Xifeng said, “Xiren isn't here, though. You should have someone send her a couple of dishes.” At this, Yuanyang ordered two dishes sent to Xiren as well. Then she asked the older servants, “Have the compartmented boxes for the wine party later been packed?” “It will probably take a little while yet,” one of them replied. “Tell them to hurry,” said Yuanyang. The servant acknowledged the order.

p.src: A large bronze tripod stood on the table. On a red sandalwood stand to the left rested a large dish of Grand View ware, containing dozens of delicate, bright-yellow Buddha's-hand citrons. From a foreign-lacquer stand on the right hung a white-jade chime carved as a pair of fish, with a little mallet beside it. Ban'er, having grown somewhat less shy, reached for the mallet to strike the chime, but the maids hurriedly stopped him. Then he wanted to eat a Buddha's hand. Tanchun selected one and gave it to him, saying, “You may play with it, but it isn't edible.” A couch stood on the east side, and from the canopied bed hung scallion-green gauze curtains embroidered on both sides with flowers, grasses, and insects. Ban'er ran over to look and said, “This one's a katydid, and this one's a grasshopper.” Granny Liu promptly slapped him and scolded, “You wretched little brat, making a filthy nuisance of yourself! They were kind enough to let you come in and look around, and already you're taking liberties.” The blow made Ban'er cry, and the others had to intervene and soothe them before the matter ended. Lady Jia looked through the gauze window into the rear courtyard for a while and said, “The parasol tree beneath the back veranda is fine too, though it is rather slender.” As they were speaking, a sudden gust of wind brought them the faint sound of drums and music. Lady Jia asked, “Whose family is celebrating a wedding? We are quite close to the street here.” Lady Wang and the others replied with a smile, “How could music from the street carry this far? Those are the dozen or so girls of our household practicing their wind instruments and percussion.” Lady Jia smiled. “If they are rehearsing, why not have them come in here and perform? They can enjoy an outing too, and we shall have more amusement.” Hearing this, Xifeng promptly sent someone to summon them, while also ordering long tables to be set out and covered with red felt. Lady Jia said, “Set them up in the waterside pavilion at Lotus Fragrance Anchorage; the sound will be lovelier over the water. Later we shall drink beneath Brocade-Adorning Pavilion, where it is spacious and the music can be heard close at hand.” Everyone agreed that it was a fine place. Lady Jia smiled at Aunt Xue. “Let us be going. These young ladies do not much care to have people sitting in their rooms, for fear they will make them dirty. Let us take the hint and go for a proper boat ride and a drink.” With that, everyone rose to leave. Tanchun laughed. “How can you say such a thing? I could not be happier if Grandmother and Aunt would honor me by sitting here awhile.” Lady Jia laughed. “This Third Girl of mine is a good one; it is only those two Jades who are insufferable. When we have drunk our fill later, we shall make a point of going to their rooms and raising a commotion.”

p.src: At this everyone laughed, and they all went out together. Before they had gone far, they reached Water-Caltrop Islet. The boatwomen selected from Suzhou had already poled over two hardwood pleasure boats. Lady Jia, Lady Wang, Aunt Xue, Granny Liu, Yuanyang, and Yuchuan were helped aboard the first, and Li Wan followed them at the rear. Xifeng boarded as well and, standing in the bow, made to pole the boat herself. From inside the cabin Lady Jia said, “This is no game. It may not be a river, but parts of it are quite deep. Come inside at once!” Xifeng laughed. “What is there to fear? Dear Ancestress, you need not worry.” With that, she planted the pole and pushed off. When they reached the middle of the pond, the small boat was so crowded that Xifeng felt it rocking wildly. She quickly handed the pole to a boatwoman and crouched down. Then Yingchun and her sisters, together with Baoyu, boarded the other boat and followed behind. The remaining old nannies and maids followed in scattered groups along the banks. Baoyu said, “These wretched withered lotus leaves are such an eyesore. Why has no one been told to pull them out?” Baochai laughed. “Has this garden had a single day's rest lately? We have been roaming through it every day. When could anyone have found the time to tidy it?” Lin Daiyu said, “I have never much cared for Li Yishan's poetry, but I do like this one line of his: ‘Leave the withered lotus to hear the rain upon it.’ And yet you insist on leaving no withered lotus at all.” Baoyu said, “It truly is a fine line. From now on, we shall not have them pulled out.” As he spoke, they reached the vine-covered inlet below Flower Creek. A chill gloom seemed to penetrate their very bones, while the withered grasses and dying water caltrops on both banks deepened the autumnal mood.

p.src: Seeing the spacious, airy pavilion on the bank, Grandmother Jia asked, “Is that your Miss Xue’s residence?” “Yes,” everyone replied. Grandmother Jia promptly ordered the boat brought alongside. They ascended the cloud-patterned stone steps and entered Alpinia Court together, where an exotic fragrance assailed their nostrils. The colder the weather grew, the greener the strange plants and immortal vines became. They were laden with charming clusters of fruit like coral beads. But when they entered the rooms, they found them as bare as a snow cave, without a single ornament anywhere. On the table stood only an earthen Ding-ware vase holding a few chrysanthemums, beside two sets of books, a tea caddy, and teacups. Only a blue gauze canopy hung over the bed, and the quilts and mattress were exceedingly plain. Grandmother Jia sighed. “This child is far too unassuming. If you have nothing with which to furnish your rooms, why not ask your aunt for some things? I paid no attention and never thought of it; naturally, your own things must have been left at home instead of being brought here.” With that, she ordered Yuanyang to fetch some antiques, then scolded Xifeng: “How stingy of you not to send your younger cousin a few ornaments!” Lady Wang, Xifeng, and the others replied with a laugh, “She would not have them herself. We did send her some, but she returned them all.” Aunt Xue also laughed. “Even at home, she never cared much for such things.” Grandmother Jia shook her head. “That will never do. She may prefer to avoid bother, but if some relative should visit, this would hardly look proper. Besides, it is considered inauspicious for a young girl’s room to be so austerely bare. At that rate, old women like us ought all the more to live in the stables! Just think of the young ladies’ boudoirs described in books and plays—how exquisitely appointed they are! Though these girls cannot presume to compare themselves with such ladies, they should not depart too far from the proper style. Why not display the things that are ready at hand? If she dearly loves simplicity, she may put out only a few pieces. I used to be the best at arranging rooms, but now that I am old, I no longer have the leisure for it. The girls have learned to arrange their rooms quite well too; the danger is that vulgar taste can spoil even fine things. But I do not find their taste vulgar. Now let me arrange your room for you, and I guarantee it will be both elegant and restrained. I have kept a couple of private treasures all this time without ever letting Baoyu see them. If he once laid eyes on them, they would be mine no longer.” She called Yuanyang over and instructed her personally: “Bring the stone miniature landscape, the gauze table screen, and the black frozen-stone incense tripod. Those three pieces on this table will be enough. Then bring the white silk bed curtains painted with ink pictures and calligraphy, and replace these curtains as well.” Yuanyang assented and said with a smile, “All those things are stored somewhere in the chests upstairs in the east wing, though I do not know which ones. We shall have to search for them at leisure, so I may as well bring them tomorrow.”

But when they entered the rooms, they found them as bare as a snow cave, without a single ornament anywhere. On the table stood only an earthen Ding-ware vase holding a few chrysanthemums, beside two sets of books, a tea caddy, and teacups.
Only a blue gauze canopy hung over the bed, and the quilts and mattress were exceedingly plain.
Grandmother Jia sighed. “This child is far too unassuming.
If you have nothing with which to furnish your rooms, why not ask your aunt for some things?
I paid no attention and never thought of it; naturally, your own things must have been left at home instead of being brought here.”
With that, she ordered Yuanyang to fetch some antiques, then scolded Xifeng: “How stingy of you not to send your younger cousin a few ornaments!”
Lady Wang, Xifeng, and the others replied with a laugh, “She would not have them herself.
We did send her some, but she returned them all.”
Aunt Xue also laughed. “Even at home, she never cared much for such things.”
Grandmother Jia shook her head. “That will never do.
She may prefer to avoid bother, but if some relative should visit, this would hardly look proper. Besides, it is considered inauspicious for a young girl’s room to be so austerely bare.
At that rate, old women like us ought all the more to live in the stables!
Just think of the young ladies’ boudoirs described in books and plays—how exquisitely appointed they are!
Though these girls cannot presume to compare themselves with such ladies, they should not depart too far from the proper style.
Why not display the things that are ready at hand?
If she dearly loves simplicity, she may put out only a few pieces.
I used to be the best at arranging rooms, but now that I am old, I no longer have the leisure for it.
The girls have learned to arrange their rooms quite well too; the danger is that vulgar taste can spoil even fine things.
But I do not find their taste vulgar.
Now let me arrange your room for you, and I guarantee it will be both elegant and restrained.
I have kept a couple of private treasures all this time without ever letting Baoyu see them. If he once laid eyes on them, they would be mine no longer.”

She called Yuanyang over and instructed her personally: “Bring the stone miniature landscape, the gauze table screen, and the black frozen-stone incense tripod. Those three pieces on this table will be enough.
Then bring the white silk bed curtains painted with ink pictures and calligraphy, and replace these curtains as well.”

Yuanyang assented and said with a smile, “All those things are stored somewhere in the chests upstairs in the east wing, though I do not know which ones. We shall have to search for them at leisure, so I may as well bring them tomorrow.”

p.src: Xifeng hurried over and said with a smile, “Since we are playing a drinking game, it would be better to have Sister Yuanyang conduct it.” Everyone knew that any game played by Grandmother Jia had to be prompted by Yuanyang, so they all agreed that this was an excellent idea. Xifeng therefore pulled Yuanyang over. Lady Wang said with a smile, “Since you are taking part in the game, you cannot very well remain standing.” Turning to a young maid, she ordered, “Bring a chair and place it at the table of your two young mistresses.” Yuanyang yielded after a show of reluctance, thanked them, sat down, and drank a cup of wine. Then she smiled and said, “The rules of a drinking game are as binding as military orders. Rank counts for nothing, and I alone am commander. Anyone who disobeys me will be punished.” Lady Wang and the others laughed. “Certainly. Now hurry and tell us the rules.” Before Yuanyang could begin, Granny Liu left her seat, waving her hands. “Do not make sport of me like this. I am going home!” Everyone laughed. “Oh no, you cannot do that!” Yuanyang commanded the young maids, “Drag her back to the table!” The young maids laughed too and duly pulled her back to her place. Granny Liu kept crying, “Have mercy on me!” Yuanyang said, “One more word, and the penalty is a whole pot.” Only then did Granny Liu fall silent. Yuanyang said, “I shall now call out sets of dominoes. We shall begin with the Old Lady, then proceed in order until we reach Granny Liu. For each set I call, I shall separate its three tiles, naming the first, then the second, and then the third; afterward I shall give the name of the complete set. You must match each call with a line—whether from poetry, song, rhapsody, an idiom, or a common saying—and every line must rhyme. Anyone who makes a mistake must drink a cup.” Everyone laughed. “That is a fine game. Call the first set!” Yuanyang said, “Here is a set. On the left is a ‘Heaven’ tile.” Grandmother Jia replied, “Above our heads spreads the blue heaven.” “Good!” everyone cried. Yuanyang said, “In the middle is a ‘Five and Six.’” Grandmother Jia replied, “By the Six Bridges, plum blossom fragrance pierces to the bone.” Yuanyang said, “The remaining tile is a ‘Six and One.’” Grandmother Jia replied, “A round red sun rises beyond the clouds.” Yuanyang said, “Together they form a ‘Dishevelled Ghost.’” Grandmother Jia replied, “This ghost clings to Zhong Kui’s leg.” When she had finished, everyone laughed and exclaimed, “Marvellous!” Grandmother Jia drank a cup. Yuanyang continued, “Here is another set. On the left is a ‘Long Five.’” Aunt Xue replied, “Plum blossoms dance before the wind, bloom after bloom.” Yuanyang said, “On the right is another ‘Five Long.’” Aunt Xue replied, “In the tenth month, plum blossoms perfume the ridge.” Yuanyang said, “The ‘Two-Five’ in the middle is the Mixed Seven.” Aunt Xue replied, “The Weaving Maid and Cowherd meet on the Seventh Night.”

p.src: Yuanyang said, “Together they form ‘Erlang Roams the Five Sacred Peaks.’” Aunt Xue replied, “No mortal knows the joy of immortals.” When she finished, everyone praised her, and she drank her wine. Yuanyang continued, “Here is another set. On the left, the ‘Long One’ shows two clear pips.” Xiangyun replied, “Twin orbs of sun and moon hang high, illuminating heaven and earth.” Yuanyang said, “On the right, the ‘Long One’ shows two clear pips.” Xiangyun replied, “Idle blossoms fall to earth without a sound.” Yuanyang said, “In the middle we still need the ‘One-Four.’” Xiangyun replied, “Beside the sun, red apricot blossoms are planted against the clouds.” Yuanyang said, “Together they form ‘Nine Ripe Cherries.’” Xiangyun replied, “Yet birds have carried them away from the imperial garden.” When she finished, she drank a cup. Yuanyang said, “Here is another set. On the left is the ‘Long Three.’” Baochai replied, “A pair of swallows chatter between the rafters.” Yuanyang said, “On the right is the ‘Three Long.’” Baochai replied, “Water weeds tugged by the wind trail long green ribbons.” Yuanyang said, “In the middle, the ‘Three-Six’ bears nine pips.” Baochai replied, “Three mountains sink halfway beyond the azure sky.” Yuanyang said, “Together they form ‘The Iron Chain Mooring the Solitary Boat.’” Baochai replied, “Wherever there are wind and waves, there too is sorrow.” When she finished, she drained her cup. Yuanyang continued, “On the left is a ‘Heaven.’” Daiyu replied, “On so fair a day, amid so lovely a scene—ah, what a heaven!” Hearing this, Baochai turned and looked at her. Daiyu was intent only on avoiding a penalty and took no notice. Yuanyang said, “In the middle, the ‘Brocade Screen’ displays its lovely colours.” Daiyu replied, “Yet no Hongniang comes to the gauze window with tidings.” Yuanyang said, “The remaining ‘Two-Six’ has all eight pips.” Daiyu replied, “Two ranks gaze upon the jade throne and lead the courtly rites.” Yuanyang said, “Together they form a ‘Basket,’ well suited for gathering flowers.” Daiyu replied, “A fragrant peony is lifted on an immortal’s staff.” When she finished, she took a sip. Yuanyang said, “On the left, ‘Four-Five’ makes a Flowery Nine.” Yingchun replied, “Peach blossoms glow richly in the rain.” Everyone cried, “A penalty! It neither rhymes nor matches the tile.” Yingchun smiled and took a sip. In fact, Xifeng and Yuanyang both wanted to hear Granny Liu’s amusing answers, so they deliberately called errors on everyone and made them drink penalties. Still, I suppose I must give it a try.” Everyone laughed. “It is easy enough. Just say whatever comes to mind; it does not matter.” Yuanyang said with a smile, “On the left, the ‘Four-Four’ is a man.” Granny Liu pondered this for a long while before saying, “Then he must be a countryman.” The whole company burst into laughter. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Well said! That is exactly how you should answer.”
